title: Harissa and Yoghurt Beef Skewers
changes_from_base: Marinated in a homemade spice harissa (toasted caraway, paprika, chilli, cumin, coriander, garlic and tomato purée) mixed with Greek yoghurt instead of the lemon-oregano marinade; meat-only skewers served with the remaining harissa as a dip, without peppers, onion or bread.
summary: These beef skewers follow the same hot-and-fast grilling method as a classic kebab, but the beef is marinated in a homemade harissa paste loosened with Greek yoghurt instead of a lemon-oregano marinade, then served meat-only with the remaining harissa as a dip.
equipment: barbecue or ridged cast-iron griddle pan
4 long metal skewers (or wooden skewers soaked 30 min)
pestle and mortar or spice grinder

ingredients.note: use half for a milder paste

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
beef sirloin (or rump), trimmed, cut into 3.5 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
lemon juice, to loosen the dip
coriander or parsley leaves, to scatter

steps.title: Toast and grind the caraway
steps.text: Toast the caraway seeds in a small dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant and nutty, then crush them coarsely with a pestle and mortar. Toasting briefly over direct heat brings out the seeds' oils; take the pan off the heat before adding anything else so the next spices don't scorch.

steps.title: Make the harissa paste
steps.text: Off the heat, stir the paprika, chilli flakes, cumin and coriander into the warm pan for about 20 seconds, letting the residual heat wake up the ground spices without burning them. Tip into a bowl and mix with the garlic, tomato purée, lemon juice, olive oil and the harissa salt to make a thick, brick-red paste.

steps.title: Marinate the beef
steps.text: Spoon about half the harissa (roughly 4 tbsp) into a bowl with the yoghurt and the beef salt, add the beef and toss until well coated. Cover and refrigerate for 1-2 hours. The yoghurt's acidity and clinginess help the paste coat the meat evenly, so it chars nicely on the grill instead of sliding off.

steps.title: Make the dip
steps.text: Stir the remaining harissa with the lemon juice in a small bowl until loosened to a dip-like consistency, then leave at room temperature until needed. This uses up the other half of the paste, so there's a punchy, spiced sauce ready for serving.

steps.title: Thread and heat
steps.text: Thread the marinated beef onto the four skewers, leaving the pieces just touching rather than squeezed together. Heat the barbecue or griddle pan over high heat until very hot before adding the skewers, so the surface sears quickly.

steps.title: Grill the skewers
steps.text: Grill for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until the edges are nicely charred and a probe thermometer in the centre of the thickest cube reads 63°C. The yoghurt and paprika in the marinade colour and darken quickly, so lower the heat slightly if the outside blackens before the centre reaches temperature.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Rest the skewers under foil for 3 minutes so the juices settle back through the meat. Scatter with coriander or parsley and serve with the harissa dip alongside.

tips: Take the pan off the heat before stirring in the ground spices — direct heat scorches paprika and turns it bitter rather than fragrant.
Don't use all the harissa in the marinade; keeping half back gives you a ready-made dipping sauce with no extra work.
If the yoghurt-coated beef starts to blacken before the centre reaches 63°C, turn the heat down slightly rather than pulling the skewers off early.
Space the beef pieces out on the skewer so heat reaches all sides evenly, rather than pushing them together.
Use a probe thermometer in the thickest cube rather than guessing by colour, since the dark harissa coating can make the beef look done before it is.
storage: Keep leftover beef and dip in separate covered containers in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat the beef gently until piping hot throughout (74°C); the dip is best served cold or at room temperature and isn't suitable for reheating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
